paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: grace is not a permission slip. Paul asks, "Shall we sin because we are not under law, but under grace?" and answers, "Certainly not!" (Romans 6:15). Grace didn't just cover the mess, it set you free from the thing making the mess.

Paul says you're "slaves to the one you obey," and he gives only two masters: sin leading to death, or obedience leading to righteousness (Romans 6:16). Nobody gets a third option, not even me standing in the middle of the bakery trying to obey nobody. The old master left you with things you're ashamed of, and Paul says "The outcome of those things is death" (Romans 6:21). But now that you've been set free, "the fruit you reap leads to holiness, and the outcome is eternal life" (Romans 6:22).

So the question for you, baker, is who gets your hands, your feet and your everyday choices today. Paul says to offer them "in slavery to righteousness leading to holiness" (Romans 6:19). And notice you aren't earning your way out, because "the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord" (Romans 6:23). Sin hands you a paycheck, but God hands you a GIFT, and that is the best deal in the whole Dorinverse.
